mappings.note: Matches traditional signs - ants, birds, pine cones - to the weather they foretell, which is observation lore rather than atmospheric theory. Not LO-6: unlike the ants item that names flooding, this one only settles on 'coming rain', so no disaster is in view.

The NDMA station at a Sikkim glacial lake exists for early warning in a hazard-prone place, which is the disaster-preparedness outcome. Not C-SST1.1, because the AWS as a device is covered by other items and here its purpose is the point.

Compares how people feel in humid Mumbai against dry Jaipur - a bodily consequence of a region's moisture. Not LO-4, because the two humidities are handed to the learner and no region has to be located.
Weighs digital against liquid-in-glass thermometers on precision and data storage - an instrument-choice item. Not LO-3, since no property of the atmosphere is explained.

Defines heat wave, cold wave, ground frost and dust storm as atmospheric phenomena and rejects the false one. Not LO-6, which is kept for items about warnings and what to do, whereas this one only settles definitions.

The three statements concern pressure falling with altitude, humidity as water vapour and the unit of wind speed - all properties of the atmosphere. Not C-SST1.1, because the km/h statement is about the quantity, not about the anemometer.
Names the atmosphere as the gaseous envelope and the answer gives its nitrogen-oxygen make-up - composition. Not LO-1, which is about picking out individual layers in a diagram.

The same temperature reads as cold in Chennai and pleasant in Kashmir because bodies are adjusted to their home climate - the climate-and-people outcome. Not LO-4, because the two climates are contrasted through their inhabitants, not located.

Identifies humidity as the environmental variable driving the pine cone. Deliberately separated from the earlier pine-cone item, which asked what the cone does and was grouped with the observation items under C-SST1.1.
Defines 'forecast' as prediction from current observations and models - the practice of meteorology. Not LO-6, because no hazardous event is involved.
Evaporative cooling through latent heat is an atmospheric moisture process. Not LO-5, because no human use of the effect is required.

Identifies the Celsius scale from its fixed points - a measurement-scale item, like the Fahrenheit conversion. Not LO-3, since freezing and boiling points are properties of water, not of the atmosphere's structure.
A museum controlling humidity to protect artefacts is a weather element governing a human activity. Not C-SST1.1, because the item never asks which instrument does the monitoring.
Finds the false instrument-function pairing, keyed on the wind sock not giving calibrated speed. Squarely an instrument item, not an LO-3 explanation.
A depression as an area of markedly lower pressure than its surroundings is atmospheric structure. Not LO-6, because the item stops before any cyclone preparation, unlike the coastal-cyclone case.
'Statistics' here means gathering and analysing observations to find patterns - the data side of meteorological practice. Not LO-3, since no atmospheric property is described.

Acclimatisation is the human body adjusting to thin, low-pressure air at altitude - people living with their environment. Not LO-3, because the physiological adjustment, not the atmosphere, is what is defined.

Heat-wave and cold-wave forecasts are valued for warning vulnerable people to take precautions - preventive action ahead of an extreme event. Not LO-5, because the answer is about the warning system, not about how people ordinarily live in that climate.
Asks what an anemometer and a wind vane actually report - instrument function, with the cockpit only as the setting. The companion item on why wind matters to aviation was given LO-5 instead.

Completes the IMD motto with 'rain', which the answer ties to solar energy driving the water cycle. Same atmospheric-process outcome as the fuller motto item; the frame has nothing narrower for the water cycle.
Sorts what a standard AWS does and does not sense, keyed on soil moisture - the scope of an instrument package. Not LO-3, because the listed parameters are not being explained.
Term-definition matching over sleet, hail, water vapour and precipitation - the moisture content of the atmosphere. Not C-SST1.1, because no device appears among the options.

Rejects rotation and keeps thermal expansion as the cause of a deeper equatorial troposphere - the structure of the atmosphere explained. Not LO-1, since the layer is named in the stem and only the mechanism is judged.
Pairs instruments with their units and rejects km/h for a barometer - measurement conventions. Not LO-3, because the item is about units rather than about pressure itself.

The keyed statement is that traditional knowledge reads animal and plant signs, which places it with the other observation-lore items. Not LO-3, because the two atmospheric statements offered are the distractors that have to be rejected.

The answer is an instrument pair - barometer and anemometer - but the task set is a cyclone early-warning system for fishermen, so it spans instrumentation and disaster preparedness. Neither code alone covers both halves.
'From rain comes food' resolves to agriculture depending on adequate rainfall - climate governing livelihood. Not LO-3, because rainfall as a process is assumed rather than explained.

Reading a weather map's legend is map interpretation, and LO-4 is the frame's only map-work outcome. Not C-SST1.1, which is kept for instruments and observation practice rather than for cartographic skill.
Defines a weather station as a site where instruments are assembled - observation infrastructure. Not LO-3, since the atmosphere is measured here, not described.
Names meteorology as the study of the atmosphere and the basis of forecasting - the discipline of observation. Not LO-3, because no specific atmospheric property is at issue.

Contrasts what a thermometer reading and a hygrometer reading each tell you - two instruments and their outputs. Not LO-3, because the item works at the level of readings rather than of air behaviour.

Interprets a dust-storm icon on a warning map into the conditions residents must expect, which is reading a hazard warning. The definitional dust-storm item was given LO-3; this one is about the warning, so the two differ.

Why the troposphere matters - it holds the air that land life breathes - is about the composition of that layer. Not LO-1, because the layer is named in the stem and its make-up, not its position, is the answer.
Puts a numeric band on relative humidity in dry weather - a quantitative property of the air. Not C-SST1.1, since no hygrometer or reading practice is involved.
Defines range of temperature as maximum minus minimum - a derived measurement, like mean daily temperature. Not LO-3, because the atmosphere itself is not being described.

A sub-1000 mb cyclone forecast and what coastal residents must prepare for is preventive action before a disaster. Not LO-3, because the pressure figure is only the trigger and the answer is the expected impact to prepare against.
One-word recall of 'atmosphere' as the gaseous envelope. Same composition outcome as its MCQ twin; LO-1 would be wrong because no individual layer is named.
Names the troposphere as the layer where weather happens - identification of an atmospheric layer, which is what LO-1 states. Not LO-3, which is used here for explanations of how that air behaves.
Names one of the five weather elements, each of which is a property of the atmosphere. Not C-SST1.1, because no instrument is asked for.
